title: Queen's Gambit Accepted
line: Black takes the offered pawn, and White gets it back with easy development.

steps.text: Black takes the offered pawn. Its center pawn has left the middle, and the pawn on c4 is hard to keep.
Bring the knight out. It guards e5, where Black's king pawn would like to strike at your center.

also.e2e4: Taking the center with the king pawn is sound too. This lesson brings the knight out first.
also.e2e3: That is sound too. This lesson brings the knight out first.

steps.after: Black brings its knight out too.

steps.text: Move the pawn in front of your king one square. Your bishop can now reach the pawn on c4.
steps.after: Black does the same and opens a path for its own bishop.

steps.text: Take the pawn back with the bishop. It comes out onto an open diagonal.
steps.after: Material is level again. Black strikes at your center pawn from the side.

steps.text: Castle. Your king is safe before the center opens.
steps.after: Black gets ready to push the pawn on b7 two squares and chase your bishop.

steps.text: Push the pawn on a2 two squares. Now a black pawn that comes to b5 can be taken, so your bishop is not chased so easily.
steps.after: White has the pawn back, a pawn in the center and a castled king.

summary: Black takes the side pawn but cannot keep it. White develops, takes it back with the bishop and keeps the center.
